newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 12.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Three followers of a religious cult murdered. The 56-year-old woman cult leader is being sought, and four cult members arrested.
- The circulation of fraudulent commercial papers amounting to 100 billion won uncovered. Twenty people involved in the fraud has been arrested. The confirmed damage reaches 20 billion won.
- Government to set up manned lighthouse in Tokto next year in a move to consolidate South Korea's occupation claim on the disputed reef islet, also claimed by Japan.
- Political consideration makes economic policy inconsistent in dealing with privatization, interest rates, greenbelt regulation, and other matters.
- Three coal miners killed, 12 trapped as drift collapsed in coal mine pit.

- Fifteen civic organizations to launch a national campaign to forestall amnesty for former presidents, Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, both awaiting the outcome of appeals to their treason and mutiny trials.
- The ruling New Korea Party, in a caucus of lawmakers yesterday, decided to retract earlier decision to act on controversial labor law revision bill within this year.
- Total foreign debt tops 100 billion dollars.
- Three miners killed, 12 buried in coal mine collapse.
